entries.text: Cross-cutting code shared by every component: clients, logging, security, telemetry. Never contains business logic.

Thin, typed wrappers over external systems; one sub-package per cloud or protocol. The only place SDK clients are constructed; every method maps SDK errors to util.exceptions and logs through the shared logger.
AWS service clients built on boto3 with one shared session factory, retries and structured error mapping.
EMR Serverless job submission and status polling.
EmrClient: start_job_run / get_job_run / cancel with typed job states.
Event publishing to the solution event bus.
EventBridgeClient: put_events with CloudEvents-shaped detail and batching.
Managed Airflow control operations: trigger, inspect and stop DAG runs.
MwaaClient: trigger_dag_run / get_dag_run / cancel via the MWAA CLI token or REST API.
Object storage operations (get/put/list/multipart, presigned URLs) for the solution buckets.
S3Client: upload/download/list/delete with server-side encryption and typed errors.
Single boto3 session/client factory with region, retry and endpoint configuration from ConfigLoader.
Queue send/receive/delete with visibility and DLQ handling.
SqsClient: send/receive/delete/batch with typed messages.
Parameter Store access for runtime configuration and secrets references.
SsmClient: get/put parameters by prefix with decryption and caching.
Azure service clients (identity, storage) for solutions that read from or deliver to Azure.
BlobClient: upload/download/list for Blob Storage / ADLS Gen2 containers with managed identity or SAS.
Relational database access: connection factory, pooled sessions, parameterised queries and transactions.
DbClient: engine/connection from ConfigLoader + secrets, execute/fetch helpers, transaction context manager. Never builds SQL from untrusted strings.
Google Cloud service clients for solutions that read from or deliver to GCP.
GcsClient: upload/download/list for Cloud Storage buckets with service-account or workload identity.
Outbound HTTP: one client with timeouts, retries with backoff, correlation-id propagation and typed errors.
RestClient: get/post/put/delete with timeout, retry, auth header injection and JSON error mapping.
SFTP transfer to and from partner servers with key-based auth and resumable uploads.
SftpClient: connect (key/password from secrets), upload/download/list with atomic rename on completion.
Structured JSON logging shared by every component; the only logger factory in the codebase.
get_logger(name) returning a structured logger with correlation-id and component fields; level from ConfigLoader; never logs PII or secrets.
Authentication and authorization helpers: token verification, subject extraction, role checks.
verify_token / current_subject / require_role helpers over the configured identity provider; raises util.exceptions.AuthError.
Audit events, metrics and tracing emitted by every component in one shape.
AuditPublisher.publish(event_type, payload) writing CloudEvents-shaped records to the configured sink; never raises into the caller's flow.
Runtime configuration: the shared base file and the loader that merges it with per-module config and environment overlays.
Base configuration shared by all modules (logging level, regions, endpoints, retry policy) with dev/staging/prod sections.
ConfigLoader: load common_config.yaml + <module>/config.yml, apply the environment section, resolve secret references via common.clients; typed accessors.
Pure helpers with no I/O: constants, exceptions, idempotency and small utilities.
Named constants shared across modules (event types, status values, header names). No magic strings elsewhere.
Domain exception hierarchy (LaminarError base; ConfigError, ClientError, NotFoundError, ConflictError, AuthError, ValidationError).
IdempotencyKey.build(*parts) and retry/backoff helpers used by APIs, lambdas and DAG tasks.
Small pure helpers (time formatting, chunking, safe JSON) used by more than one module.
All serverless function handlers of the solution plus their shared configuration. One module per function.
Function configuration per environment (timeouts, batch sizes, destination names, feature flags), loaded through ConfigLoader.
All Airflow / MWAA DAG definitions of the solution plus their shared configuration. Deployed as-is to the DAGs bucket.
Schedules, retries, SLAs, connection ids and per-DAG parameters per environment, loaded through ConfigLoader.
All Spark / EMR job modules of the solution; one sub-package per job component.
One Spark job: entrypoint, I/O, processors, transforms, configuration and recipes.
Job configuration and declarative recipes.
Job configuration per environment: sources, sinks, Spark conf, recipe directory, PII policy references.
Declarative extract/transform recipes (one JSON per product/dataset) interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Contact Method Subscription dataset interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Enriched Campaign Reactions dataset interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Enriched Campaigns dataset interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Pii Restricted Profile dataset interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Restaurant reservation dataset interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Room stay reservation dataset interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Spa treatment reservation dataset interpreted by the processors.
Declarative extract/transform recipe for the Tee time reservation dataset interpreted by the processors.
Spark runtime helpers (session construction, Spark conf) with no job logic.
get_spark_session(app_name, config) applying Spark conf, Hive/Glue catalog and S3 committer settings.
All reads and writes against external systems, one module per system. No business logic; returns/accepts DataFrames.
JDBC reads (partitioned) and writes against the relational source/sink using credentials from common.clients.db / secrets.
Read/write Parquet/CSV/JSON datasets on S3 with partitioning and manifest writing.
Job entrypoint: argument parsing, SparkSession via helper, config/recipe loading, orchestration of processors and I/O, exit codes and audit events.
Job step logic: shape inputs, apply business rules (e.g. PII handling, projections), assemble outputs. One processor per concern.
Validate and normalise the input DataFrames (schema enforcement, type casting, filtering by job parameters).
Assemble the final output datasets (ordering, partition columns, manifests, metrics) before I/O writes.
Reusable, stateless DataFrame transformers driven by recipe/config; no I/O.
Default column mapping / renaming / derivation transformer applied when a recipe names no specific transformer.
Job-local pure helpers and constants.
Job constants (column names, partition keys, status values).
Path building, manifest/file naming and small file helpers (no Spark dependency).
All serverless function handlers of the solution plus their shared configuration. One module per function.
Function configuration per environment (timeouts, batch sizes, destination names, feature flags), loaded through ConfigLoader.
lambda_handler plus the function's operations: event parsing with the designed schema, client calls through common.clients, error mapping, audit events.
All Airflow / MWAA DAG definitions of the solution plus their shared configuration. Deployed as-is to the DAGs bucket.
Schedules, retries, SLAs, connection ids and per-DAG parameters per environment, loaded through ConfigLoader.
The DAG definition: default_args, schedule from config, tasks in the designed sequence, dependencies, callbacks publishing audit events.
All Airflow / MWAA DAG definitions of the solution plus their shared configuration. Deployed as-is to the DAGs bucket.
Schedules, retries, SLAs, connection ids and per-DAG parameters per environment, loaded through ConfigLoader.
The DAG definition: default_args, schedule from config, tasks in the designed sequence, dependencies, callbacks publishing audit events.
All Airflow / MWAA DAG definitions of the solution plus their shared configuration. Deployed as-is to the DAGs bucket.
Schedules, retries, SLAs, connection ids and per-DAG parameters per environment, loaded through ConfigLoader.
The DAG definition: default_args, schedule from config, tasks in the designed sequence, dependencies, callbacks publishing audit events.
All REST/API modules of the solution; one sub-package per API component plus the shared API configuration.
API-wide configuration (host, port, CORS, auth issuer, rate limits) per environment, loaded through ConfigLoader.
One API component: entrypoint, routes, service, schemas and wiring for a single bounded context.
Application factory: creates the app, registers routers and middleware, wires dependencies, exposes health endpoint.
Dependency providers: ConfigLoader, AuditPublisher, common.clients instances, current subject (auth); single construction point.
HTTP route handlers exactly as in the design skeleton (method, path, status codes, auth dependency); delegates to service.py; maps domain exceptions to HTTP errors.
Request/response and domain models (pydantic) named as in the design document's Schema Definitions.
Business operations behind the routes: validation, orchestration of clients, idempotency, audit publishing. No HTTP types.
The single Terraform root module of the solution. Infrastructure is grouped by service type, configured per environment through values.yaml.
Providers, required versions and locals (cfg = yamldecode(values.yaml)[var.env]). Platform-owned.
Per-environment values: dev/staging/prod → resource name → settings. Merged from component fragments.
env (dev|staging|prod), project_name and provider region variables. Platform-owned.
